Automatic visual and audible alarms set to activate at 500 ppm CO concentration should be installed in such areas. 19. Employees working in high-risk CO areas must be informed of the hazards, symptoms of acute CO poisoning, and emergency evacuation procedures, with periodic drills conducted at least every six months. 20. Adequate fire extinguishing agents must be available in areas where CO is stored or used, as CO can burn and become explosive when mixed with air at certain concentrations. 21. Each CO storage container must be inspected for leaks upon arrival or filling and reexamined at least every three months. 22. Before transferring CO from storage containers, inspections must be conducted to detect gas leaks in the transport system. 23. 24. Monitoring frequency should be at least annual, with more frequent monitoring considered under specific circumstances, such as process changes or seasonal variations. 25. 26. The National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) has developed criteria for standards to protect employees from hazardous chemical and physical agents, including CO. 27. The document emphasizes that recommended standards should guide the development of better engineering controls and healthier work practices, rather than being considered a final goal. 28. 29. CO is an odorless, colorless, tasteless gas primarily encountered as a byproduct of incomplete combustion of carbonaceous materials. 30. CO binds with hemoglobin to form carboxyhemoglobin (COHb), reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity and leading to hypoxia. 31. Acute CO poisoning is a leading cause of toxic agent-related fatalities, second only to alcohol. 32. 33. 34. 35. 36.
